    Round I · while coding
    Implementation assumptions
    Where the ticket was ambiguous: the reading the coder chose.
    1. assumption60% confident Unknown vetId is a 404 on GitHub ↗  in VS Code
      Read the other way: 400 naming vetId as the bad field
      Why 60%: Matches how unknown pet types are handled. A 400 is more correct HTTP, which is why this is close to a coin flip.
      

      2. 

    2. assumption60% confident Deleting a vet keeps their visits, with no vet on GitHub ↗  in VS Code
      Read the other way: refuse deleting a vet who has visits
      Why 60%: Ticket item 4 makes "no vet" a normal state, and before this change vet deletion always succeeded. Losing who attended is a real history loss, so a business owner could reasonably pick refusal.
      

      3. 

    3. assumption65% confident Seed gives a vet to some demo visits only on GitHub ↗  in VS Code
      Read the other way: leave every seeded visit without a vet
      Why 65%: The demo should show both states; ticket item 4 is about real legacy rows, not the demo dataset.
      R__seed.sql
      

      4. 

    4. assumption70% confident PUT replaces the visit; a missing vetId means no vet on GitHub ↗  in VS Code
      Read the other way: PATCH-like: absent keeps the vet, explicit null clears it
      Why 70%: Ticket item 2 makes "clear must stick" the priority, and full-replace PUT is the simplest rule that guarantees it; the only client, our edit form, always sends the field. Four reviewers flagged the omitted-field case, which pulls confidence down.
      

      5. 

    5. assumption70% confident MCP create_visit takes no vet; list_visits shows it on GitHub ↗  in VS Code
      Read the other way: also add a vet parameter to create_visit
      Why 70%: "Everywhere" in the ticket covers displaying, which list_visits does; choosing a vet at booking stays a staff action in the UI.
      

      6. 

    6. assumption75% confident "No vet" is the wording for a visit without one on GitHub ↗  in VS Code
      Read the other way: "—" or "Not assigned"
      Why 75%: Ticket item 4 rules out "Unknown" and blank; "No vet" says "has none" literally, and the same label serves as the combo placeholder.

    Issue #37: Link Visit with Vet
    victorrenteaon Jun 13, 2026!
    The Visit should be linked to the vet that attended that consultation. Visit should display its vet everywhere throughout the app.
    What it has to do
    1. Booking a visit lets you choose the vet, and lets you not choose one. The vet is optional: half the time the appointment is booked before anyone knows who is taking it, and forcing a choice there produces bad data rather than information.
    2. Editing a visit can change the vet, and can remove it. Clearing the field must persist as empty. We had this with pet types: the old value kept coming back.
    3. Wherever a visit is shown with its details, the vet is shown too. Today that means the owner's page and the all-visits screen.
    4. A visit with no vet reads as having none. Not "Unknown", not blank-because-broken, and never an error. Visits created before this change have no vet and will not get one.
    Out of scope
    Searching or filtering visits by vet.
    fully coveredpartiallyexecutedmissingN/A
